newsitem.title: UK: Zinc to reach $1,320 by end of 1997 - MBR.
newsitem.headline: Zinc to reach $1,320 by end of 1997 - MBR.

text.p: Zinc prices are expected to reach 60 cents a pound ($1,320/tonne) by the end of next year as stocks start to fall towards critically low levels, said Tariq Salaria, analyst for Metal Bulletin Research (MBR).
Addressing the London Metal Exchange (LME) metals seminar on Monday, he said world zinc stocks should fall to below six weeks' worth of consumption by late 1997.
"We believe a move to below 6 weeks' worth (consumption) should occur by end-1997 when things start to become critical and equate to a price around $1,320/tonne," he said.
Salaria said zinc stocks now were around eight weeks' offtake, with the LME stockpile equating to around 4.5 weeks'.

"Historically prices have only started to move once total stocks have fallen below seven weeks' worth of consumption, implying a further 120,000 tonne decline prior to any marked improvement," he said.
Values may also rise because of the re-emergence of investment fund buying and the potential for zinc stocks to be concentrated among a small number of market participants.
Demand for zinc in 1996 was weak, declining two percent in the West this year after two years of growth above five percent.
Mine production was expected to continue to grow at around four percent annually between 1996 and 1998, with new projects coming on stream around the globe.
But refined production rises have yet to match the increase in mine production.
Salaria said the glut in concentrates and higher treatment charges for smelters would lead to a higher utilisation rate among smelters from the current level of 87 percent.
Chinese exports to the West in 1996 will be limited by low prices and rising domsetic demand.
Net exports from the former Eastern Bloc to the West are forecast to fall from 460,000 tonnes in 1995, although further ahead the trend is likely to return to rising exports.
"By 1998, due primarily to higher Chinese smelter production, the surplus in East Bloc exports is forecast to move upwards again," Salaria said.
